conviction_note: Nothing decisive and nothing the market has not seen: a mild upward lean (p_up 54) from an inaugural buyback announced after the quarter closed, consensus cut 2.6% in 30 days, a stock 10.7% below its July print and benign peer credit, set against a $0.83 EPS bar that needs about 7.5% core net-income growth over a Q2 flattered by a $1.9M interest recovery; abs_move 4.0 is the name's 2.61% median scaled up for a regional-bank print with a 14.6% and a -6.8% tail and no usable option chain; findings sum to +0.6 and the scaled number is +0.32, the same sign at about half the size, because p_up carries the uncertainty the findings do not.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS $0.83 (post 2-for-1 split, effective 2026-08-20) and revenue $173.15M: Earnings Whispers https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/SFBS and the Zacks-sourced FMP preview https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/market-news/servisfirst-bancshares-sfbs-q3-2026-earnings-preview-stock-buyback (estimate down 2.6% over 30 days). Benzinga carries $0.82 and $175.0M https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SFBS/earnings-forecasts. Two sources agree to within a cent. There is no company guidance beyond call commentary: mid-teens loan growth for the rest of 2026 and a slower pace of NIM expansion. Compare Q2 2026 at $1.57 pre-split ($0.785 post), revenue $168.5M, NII $155.6M, NIM 3.63% including a 5bp one-off.
positioning_check: Short interest 6,161,384 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up 496,466 from the prior period. That is about 5.6% of shares outstanding (a higher share of float, since insiders hold a large stake), with 7.49 days to cover on about 823k shares a day. Source: https://equibles.com/stocks/sfbs/shortinterest, read 2026-10-19. The 15 October figure is not out until 26 October. This is moderately elevated and rising for a bank: not a crowded short, but it leans toward a squeeze on a clean print. There is no skew: the baseline option chain is empty (options.status empty_chain). A third-party page quotes an implied move of +/-11.2%, which looks unreliable on an empty chain and is not used. On the tape the stock is -6.39% over 20 days, +1.32% over 5 days, 14.26% below its 52-week high, and -10.7% since the 2026-07-20 print according to Earnings Whispers.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-14, five days before the print and after the quarter had closed on 2026-09-30, the board approved the company's first-ever buyback of up to 2 million shares (about 1.8% of roughly 109.3M post-split shares) through 2027-12-31, citing 'confidence' in the company's 'financial strength, capital position'. Management therefore announced it already knowing Q3, which is a mild sign the quarter does not contain a large credit or margin surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the company's first buyback, so there is no history on this line. Over the 5 sessions that include the announcement the stock rose +1.32% (baseline run_up_5d_pct).
findings.why_not_priced: The announcement itself is public and the sweep lists it as in the wire, so the buyback is partly priced. What is less priced is its timing as a signal about Q3, a quarter already closed. Had the market fully read that signal, the stock would not still sit 10.7% below its July print with estimates being cut; it has recovered only 1.3% over five days.
findings.independence: None from a different source. The finviz copy of the same release (https://finviz.com/news/402642/servisfirst-bancshares-inc-announces-inaugural-stock-repurchase-program) is the same document.

findings.finding: The $0.83 EPS bar is not easy. It equals about $90.7M of net income on roughly 109.3M shares, against Q2's $85.8M. Q2 included a $1.9M recovery of interest income from a large nonaccrual relationship (5bp of NIM), so core net income has to grow about 7.5% quarter on quarter while the revenue consensus ($173.15M against Q2's $168.5M) grows only about 2.8%. That only works if the provision ($11.4M in Q2) falls or the efficiency ratio (29.65%) improves.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 missed EPS at $1.30 against $1.38 and revenue as well, and the stock fell 6.8% (https://finviz.com/news/198010/servisfirst-bancshares-sfbs-lags-q3-earnings-and-revenue-estimates). Q2 2026 was in line on EPS with a 0.7% NII miss: the stock was +5.6% right after the report, +2.61% over the scored window and -10.7% since.
findings.why_not_priced: The 30-day estimate cut of 2.6% shows the street already drifting toward this. The gap left is the one-off in the Q2 base, which a headline comparison of $0.785 against $0.83 does not strip out. If it were priced, consensus would sit nearer $0.80-0.81.
findings.independence: This is my own arithmetic on the Q2 release plus the consensus at https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/SFBS. It shares the Q2 release with the loan-growth finding, which pulls the other way.

findings.finding: Q2 ending loans rose $532.6M (15.3% annualised) to $14.48B and the pipeline was a record. Management guided mid-teens loan growth for the rest of the year, so Q3 average loans start about $250-300M above the Q2 average before any new growth. That supports NII growth beyond the 2.8% in the revenue consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print (2026-01-20) was a growth and NIM quarter and moved +14.58%. Q2 combined strong loan growth with an in-line result and moved +2.61%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it sits inside what management guided, so I sized it toward zero. What may be under-modelled is the lift from ending to average balances, given that the revenue consensus implies under 3% growth.
findings.independence: This is the same Q2 release as the bar finding. The guidance is quoted in MarketBeat's call summary: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/servisfirst-bancshares-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-20/

findings.finding: Peer read from Regions' Q3 2026 release (2026-10-16), a Southeast regional bank: NIM +2bp to 3.68%, net charge-offs down to 0.29% from 0.42%, NPLs down to 0.59% from 0.67%, criticized business loans down, but loan growth of only 0.6% and higher non-deposit funding costs after the September rate rise. Credit is benign across the region and margins are still expanding modestly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-level history for a peer read-through. SFBS's own negative reaction (-6.8%, Q3 2025) came on a miss together with credit migration.
findings.why_not_priced: Regions reported after SFBS last spoke, but a large peer's improving credit is a sector fact the market can already see. It is a proxy: SFBS's own risk is one large real-estate relationship, not region-wide migration.
findings.independence: This is a proxy. The Newsquawk headline (https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/regions-financial-rf-q3-2026-usd-adj-eps-073-exp-066) shows adjusted EPS of $0.73 against $0.66 expected, which is the same event.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, the first hike since 2023. SFBS funds $1.58B with federal funds purchased (correspondent banks, repriced immediately) and pays 2.80% on interest-bearing deposits, a high-beta base. Q4 NIM commentary could therefore come in below the 4-6bp a quarter suggested in July, although prime-based loans also reprice. The sign is uncertain.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM is the line this stock trades on: +14.58% on the Q4 2025 print, and the Q2 2026 NIM beat of 4bp was met with +5.6% right after the report. The company gives no formal guidance, only call commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: Transmission from macro to the company is unconfirmed by SFBS. The hike itself is fully public. Regions named higher non-deposit funding costs as an offset, the funding line where SFBS is most exposed. If it were priced, the stock's 20-day decline would be the evidence, but that has other plausible causes.
findings.independence: Regions' release (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026) cites higher non-deposit funding costs. The FOMC outcome is corroborated at https://www.atfx.com/en-au/analysis/financial-events/september-fomc-meeting-2026-is-a-rate-hike-on-the-table. The heygotrade page is partly AI-generated, so this is a weak source.

findings.finding: Nonperforming loans were $171.0M (1.18% of loans) at Q2 against $72.2M a year earlier, driven by one large real-estate relationship that also produced the $1.9M Q2 interest recovery. Q3 could bring either a resolution (another recovery and an NPL drop) or a charge-off. Nothing public shows which.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (-6.8%) coincided with the NPL build. The lumpy reactions (+14.6% and -6.8%) suggest this line can dominate a print.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is unknowable from public sources, so this is filed at zero as a known source of variance and widens abs_move rather than the sign. No Alabama court filing was found.
findings.independence: Critics of the NPL rise are summarised at https://www.webull.com/news/15267887976571904. That is the same underlying data.

findings.finding: Expectations and positioning have reset. The stock is -10.7% since the July print and 14.3% below its 52-week high, consensus EPS fell 2.6% in 30 days, and short interest rose to 6.16M shares (about 5.6% of shares outstanding, 7.5 days to cover) at 2026-09-30. The bar has been lowered into a print that history shows is usually positive (5 of 7 up).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 5 of 7 prior reactions were positive and the median absolute move is 2.61% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not new information. It only pays if the print clears a bar the market has already lowered. If the reset were complete, short interest would be falling and estimates stable.
findings.independence: https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/SFBS (-10.7% since the last report, $0.83 consensus) is a different source for the drift.

findings.finding: Director J. Richard Cashio sold 11,500 shares on 2026-07-31 at $89.43 pre-split, after selling 42,000 in March. No insider Form 4 purchases or sales are on EDGAR for September or October 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: This is old and public, and a single director's routine sale carries little weight. Its absence of follow-on activity in Sep-Oct is mildly neutral.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The mild positive lean cuts against the -6.4% 20-day run-up and the falling estimates, but it rests on that same reset (a lowered bar), so it is contrarian only in a small way.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown and positioning are worth little): the positioning/reset finding went from +0.5 to +0.3, because it rests on the absence of a cause rather than on a document.

Rule 6: checked the bar against two agreeing sources ($0.83 at Earnings Whispers and Zacks/FMP, $0.82 at Benzinga), so findings were not capped. The loan-growth finding was already sized toward zero as inside the guide.
Rule 5 (macro transmission is a small finding): the Fed-hike finding stays at -0.3 with a proxy label, unchanged.
Nothing else changed: p_up and abs_move are unchanged.
